verification_report.summary: Correct under the explicitly accepted internal inputs. The shortened zero-exponent proof is noncircular: after the retained Gauduchon, Skoda, reference-preserving subsolution, scalar-order, and exponential-order estimates establish a common interval V_theta-B<=v_j<=V_theta and two-sided scalar bounds, it uses only normalized qpsh compactness and cor:big-reference-uniform-convergence. The displayed densities then converge strongly in L^p to cf, which identifies the cluster equation; scalar order uniquely determines c without asserting potential uniqueness. For all 0<lambda<=1, the proposition correctly obtains uniform scalar and type bounds, with every comparison orientation verified. The fixed lower bound gives whole-family strong L^p density convergence as lambda tends to zero on the complement of the analytic pole set, never subtracting common infinite values. Fixed-reference compactness identifies every cluster equation and scalar, while the uniform local Holder theorem plus interpolation gives one subsequence converging on every compact in every strict sub-endpoint C^beta topology. The symmetry corollary correctly uses pullback naturality, envelope invariance of V_theta, positive-exponent uniqueness in the minimal type, and L^1 continuity of composition; it does not require invariance of the chosen barrier or Omega. Whole-family potential convergence is asserted only under uniqueness in the G-invariant normalized minimal class. No bounded-mass or positive-lower-mass property, and no new external theorem, is used.
